title: 1. The idea: carriers, formats and design rules

sections.name: question
sections.label: Question
sections.content: Which file formats can carry an SRS repository so that a person reads the document as usual and an SRS reader also gets its records and sources?

sections.name: answer
sections.label: What we found
sections.content:
An SRS archive (.srs) is a deterministic ZIP, and a .srsj is one JSON file, so any format that can hold a file can hold a repository.
- PDF/A-3: attach the .srs as an associated file (Root /AF, AFRelationship /Source, a media type on the embedded file). This is the pattern of electronic invoices (Factur-X / ZUGFeRD): structured data inside the document people read. Best for formal records.
- HTML: a .srsj in <script type="application/vnd.srs+json">, inert to the browser; the page can ship its own small reader. Best for the web. Weak in email and after 'Save page as'.
- DOCX: a binary part or a customXml part in the package. Weakest: Word drops unknown parts on save, and the format invites edits that make page and record disagree.
- Also: EPUB, .eml attachments, and C2PA Content Credentials on a recording (a checksum of the archive in an assertion).
- Not ZIP polyglots: fragile, and the next PDF save breaks them.

sections.name: rules
sections.label: Design rules proposed
sections.content:
1. Embed the travelling form unchanged (the .srs bytes), never unpacked into the host's own ZIP, so its checksum survives.
2. Find the payload by content, not filename: file.srs.pdf is a hint for people; the operating system still opens it as a PDF.
3. Bind the visible layer to the payload: record which composition and engine produced the page, so a reader can re-render and compare.
4. Redact by tombstone: a source document whose sidecar is present but content absent is valid, so minutes can ship without the audio and still name exactly which transcript they came from.
The media type application/vnd.semanticops.srs+zip and the XMP namespace https://srs.semanticops.com/ns/carrier/1.0/ used in the prototypes are placeholders, not agreed.
